My name is Keyes Williamson. I live at 180 Plum Nelly Road (In House District 117 and Senate District 046) I believe there should be a non-partisan commission appointed to draw up political districts in Georgia, because the party in power cannot be trusted to do it in a fair and equitable way. The Democrats did it unfairly in 2000 and the Republicans did it unfairly in 2006 and after the 2010 census. The fact of the matter is that any American who truly believes in Democracy, must reject the gerrymandering of political districts to benefit one political party over another. It is a direct violation of the principles upon which our country was built; and it contradicts good common sense. When Governor Nathan Deal signed the current Congressional redistricting map, he said ""The Legislature has drawn districts that are compact, that keep communities of interest together and that visually make sense."" Athens, our community, is divided into two state districts, three state House districts, and two U.S. Congressional districts. Does this pass the smell test suggested by the Governor himself? No. We are the smallest county in the state, how does it make sense to divide it, if it is not intended to split our community's political voice for partisan reasons. As a result, our city cannot fairly select a representative to the state or U.S. legislatures that will represent the values of this community and to advocate for those issues that are important to the majority of our community members: better police policy, lower crime, better schools, less economic disparity, etc. We all know, because it is obvious, that Athens was split to manipulate the vote to predetermine the outcome of the election. If you look back at the results of past elections, you can see the swing from one party to another, not based on the qualifications of the candidates or the popularity of their platforms, the results are driven by the arbitrary and partisan districting maps. In the words of political professor Charles Bullock, the party in power was ""drawing Clarke County to benefit themselves."" This is un-American. History is not on the side of those who defend legislative districts drawn to dilute the will of the people. It is clear that the founding fathers would frown upon the kinds of districts we have in Georgia. James Madison warned the Constitution Convention that state legislatures would ""mold their regulations to favor candidates they wished to succeed."" He called this an ""abuse"" of power. President Harrison, in 1891, called the practice ""political robbery"" that suppressed ""popular suffrage."" It was, he said, ""our chief national danger."" The practice of splitting voters to predetermine elections, is, in short, at odds with our constitution and the values that make America unique. From the Declaration of Independence to the Constitution, elected democracy was constructed upon the principle that EVERY VOTE MATTERS. The current districts in Athens violate that sacred principle.

Good evening, and thank you for allowing me to speak. My name is Martha Saunders and I am here with 2 other women from Carroll County. We share several concerns about the redistricting process. Will we be able to see drafts of maps as soon as they are drawn and be able to publicly react to the drafts? We are especially interested in how the districts for the Georgia House seats are drawn. Carroll County is currently represented by 4 different House representatives, only one of whom calls Carroll County home, and he also represents part of another county. So there is no House legislator whose sole responsibility is our county's welfare and interests. Compactness and the preservation of existing political communities are two of the criteria for drawing legislative districts. We ask that the Joint Apportionment and Redistricting Committee make the system transparent and allow all citizens to see and react to all the district maps that involve their counties-Congressional, State Senate, State House, and those within the county. We appreciate your taking time to hear our concerns. We know that you have a difficult task ahead of you.

A key requirement of re-districting is to keep ""Communities of Interest"" together so that their representative can ACTUALLY represent those interests. In the re-districting that occurred in 2011, Athens-Clarke County's two democratic House districts were gerrymandered into three districts, only one of which was contained wholly in ACC (118). The other two districts (117 & 119) were combined with rural counties adjacent to ACC, guaranteeing Republican victories in those two districts. For 7 years, no democrat would even run in those two districts as they knew it was a waste of money and effort. In 2017, both republican incumbents were appointed to state offices and a special election was called. For the first time in 7 years we had Democratic candidates willing to run and they won! Obviously, the rural Republican voters didn't bother to show up for that special election but did so in record numbers in 2018, once again, guaranteeing Republican victories for House districts 117 and 119. These victories were repeated in 2020 despite record turnouts from both parties. The representatives for HD 117 and 118 do NOT represent the values and interests of the 70% of ACC residents that did NOT vote for them. Athens is an urban district (the fifth largest urban area in Georgia with over 120,000 residents in the smallest county by geography in Georgia). The needs and values of this urban county are different from those of the other rural 60% of these two districts. I urge the two committees to return ACC to two House Districts, fully contained within ACC and to also adjust the Senate districts so that only one senator can fully represent the needs of ACC instead of having ACC split between two rural senate districts. Thank you for considering this request and I hope both committees can put Partisanship aside and let the voters choose their representatives instead of the party in power choosing their voters!
